summary: Unexpected privileged account linking after legacy alt_id sync job
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:12 UTC, the security monitoring pipeline flagged multiple 'identity_merge' audit events originating from the "altid-sync-v1" job. Several merges linked contractor / vendor SSO identities with internal privileged user accounts, granting those contractor identities membership in high-privilege groups (admin, infra-sre) unexpectedly.

Impact: 12 affected accounts observed with merged memberships; 3 of those accounts gained access to infra-critical groups (able to view infra secrets and some console admin routes). No evidence of external token compromise found so far. Customer-facing systems were unaffected, but potential internal data access exposure requires immediate containment and forensics.

Timeline: 
- 2026-03-10 02:58 UTC: alt_id batch import started (scheduled job).
- 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: Security alerts for identity_merge spikes; on-call alerted.
- 2026-03-10 03:18 UTC: Identity sync job paused.
- 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Initial containment: service-account keys rotated, affected sessions revoked.

Environment: prod-us-east, identity-sync cluster (k8s), version: iam-sync v1.6.2 (legacy), auth-service v2.1.0.

Steps to reproduce / what ran: 
1. Legacy HR CSV ingestion pipeline (third-party) produced a payload to adag-identity-import queue.
2. altid-sync-v1 consumed the message and ran normalization + dedupe logic.
3. A normalization edge case treated domain aliasing and alt_email fields as canonical identifiers and executed a merge path rather than a create/path that would require manual reconciliation.

Logs (excerpt): 
- 2026-03-10T03:11:59Z altid-sync-v1 INFO ingest message id=a8f3
- 2026-03-10T03:12:07Z altid-sync-v1 WARN normalization: suspect domain-alias match for 'alex.brown@rw-inference.co' vs 'alex.brown@rw-inference.com'
- 2026-03-10T03:12:09Z auth-service INFO identity_merge user=alex.brown merged_from=vendor:contractor-392 merged_into=rw-inference/alex.brown target_groups=[infra-sre,admin]
- 2026-03-10T03:12:12Z security-monitoring ALERT high-privilege-group-change count=1 source=altid-sync-v1

Initial hypothesis: malformed / intentionally-crafted alternate-email fields in third-party HR payload caused the legacy sync to equate distinct identities; the merge code path applied memberships from the vendor identity to the internal identity without re-checking group membership policies. Given the third-party origin, this could be either accidental bad data or an attempt at targeted account linking (phishing/poisoned HR feed).
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-10T03:25Z: On-call noticed multiple identity_merge audit entries and escalated to Security. Paused altid-sync job and creating ticket.
Jordan Patel (Assignee) 2026-03-10T03:40Z: Rotated altid-sync service-account keys and revoked all idle SSO sessions. Running identity-diff to enumerate all merges since 2026-03-01.
SRE-Triage 2026-03-10T04:05Z: Confirmed job pause via k8s cronjob disable (cronjob/altid-sync paused). Snapshotting etcd and exporting identity audit log slice for forensics.

Security (Lina Ortiz) 2026-03-10T05:12Z: Observed matching IPs for ingestion queue producer belong to third-party HR vendor IP range. Reached out to vendor security contact to request raw payloads and signing keys.

Identity-Eng (Priya Rao) 2026-03-10T06:00Z: Found normalization rule that treats domain alias map as canonical; adding conditional check to avoid auto-merge for identities originating from 'vendor:' namespace. Preparing hotfix branch.
investigation_notes:
Evidence collected: export of identity audit log (events 03:10-03:20 UTC) and message queue payloads retained; pcap not available for third-party endpoint. Forensic findings: merges were triggered by a sequence where 'external_email' matched after lowercasing + domain-alias normalization. Merge path did not validate SSO fingerprint or require admin confirmation for group changes. No suspicious external token usage observed (auth logs show merges performed by service account altid-sync-v1).

Hypotheses prioritized: 
1) Maliciously crafted HR feed that intentionally set alt_email to target internal privileged principals (high risk).
2) Accidental bad data from vendor HR system using domain aliases and deprecated email fields (medium risk).
3) Internal code regression in normalization logic triggered by recent config change (low risk but being validated).

Actions taken so far: paused legacy job, rotated service account keys, revoked active sessions for affected users, snapshot of identity DB taken, notified vendor, and started an emergency audit of group membership changes for the past 30 days. Collected raw ingestion payloads and stored in secure evidence bucket.

Next investigative steps: validate vendor payloads signatures, run a full membership diff for all accounts that had merges, search for IAM elevation sequences following merges, and verify whether any secrets or console actions were performed by merged contractor accounts. Considered creating a watchlist and MFA enforcement for newly merged accounts.
resolution:
Mitigation in progress: legacy altid-sync has been paused and will remain disabled until fix is deployed. A hotfix (PR 412) introduced a policy that prevents auto-merges when origin namespace is 'vendor:' and requires manual reconciliation for any merge that would add a privileged group membership. Service account keys were rotated and an org-wide forced SSO reauth was triggered for affected accounts.

Workarounds / short-term controls: 1) Block vendor ingestion queue until signed payloads verified. 2) Add automated alert to security-monitoring for any future identity_merge events that add high-privilege groups. 3) Manual review of the 12 affected accounts and removal of inappropriate group memberships where necessary.

Follow-ups / long-term remediation: 
- INT-834211: Post-incident review and external vendor coordination (scheduled).
- Implement strict schema validation for HR/boarding feeds and require signed payloads (owner: Identity-Eng).
- Add a pre-merge policy check that enforces contract vs internal namespace separation and require admin approval for merges that touch admin/infra groups.
- Update runbooks and add acceptance tests for domain-alias normalization.

Legal/Compliance: Incident logged with Legal; we may need breach notification depending on forensics outcome.
